themes.name: Letting AI make calls, safely

themes.name: Reaching me on my phone
themes.blurb: Getting results, alerts and long documents from a terminal on a server to an iPhone, and getting replies back.

themes.name: A second brain the AI can read

themes.name: Voice in, voice out

themes.name: Documents that explain themselves

skill.label: AI skill
skill.explain: Instructions an AI agent loads when a task calls for them, like a recipe card.

hook.label: Agent hook
hook.explain: A script that runs automatically at a moment in an AI session (before a command, when it stops) to steer or guard it.

slash-command.label: Slash command
slash-command.explain: A shortcut typed into the AI chat, like /afk, that kicks off a saved routine.

subagent.label: Sub-agent
subagent.explain: A specialist AI persona the main agent can hand a job to.

mcp-server.label: MCP server
mcp-server.explain: A plug that gives AI agents a new ability, such as reading a task board or placing a call, through a standard protocol.

cli.label: Command-line tool
cli.explain: A small program run from the terminal.

api.label: API
api.explain: A service other programs can call.

model.label: Model
model.explain: A trained AI model or a configuration of one.

prompt.label: Prompt
prompt.explain: Wording that reliably gets an AI to behave a certain way.

technique.label: Technique
technique.explain: A pattern or hard-won lesson, written down so it isn't learned twice.

util.label: Browser tool
util.explain: A single web page you can use right now, no install.

artifact.label: Living document
artifact.explain: A self-contained HTML document that carries its own editing instructions.

library.label: Library
library.explain: Reusable code other projects build on.

plugin.label: Plugin
plugin.explain: An add-on that extends another tool.

automation.label: Automation
automation.explain: Something that runs on a schedule by itself.

note.label: Note
note.explain: A page from the personal wiki.

other.label: Thing
other.explain: Hard to categorize, still worth keeping.

skill-artifact.title: Artifact skill: self-describing HTML documents with embedded DSL
skill-artifact.summary_plain: Makes documents (roadmaps, logs, notes) as single web pages that carry their own editing instructions, so any person or AI can update them years later.
skill-artifact.how_it_works: Claude designs a per-task DSL; the HTML embeds the grammar, a textarea source pane and a live vanilla-JS renderer, plus a 'copy markdown bundle' for agent handoff; publish/expire slash commands and a daily launchd expiry job.

skill-html.title: HTML artifacts skill (dark-mode-first)
skill-html.summary_plain: Turns AI answers into polished one-page visual reports, decks and diagrams you can read on your phone.
skill-html.how_it_works: Single shared CSS-variable design system, adaptive dark/light, extends Thariq's html-effectiveness patterns; config.json sets Taildrop target and blog repo.

skill-director.title: Director: Mission Control fleet dispatch
skill-director.summary_plain: One command reads everything on the to-do board and opens a pre-briefed AI assistant for each area of work, side by side in the terminal.
skill-director.how_it_works: Pulls the Mission Control claimable queue + session log, buckets tasks by a workstreams.json roster, writes a manifest that director-spawn.sh fans out into tiled tmux panes each running an interactive claude seeded with a persona brief.

skill-email.title: Email skill (himalaya across seven accounts)
skill-email.summary_plain: Lets the AI read, search, file and send email across all of James's inboxes from the terminal.
skill-email.how_it_works: himalaya v2 CLI with XOAUTH2 via Workspace service accounts and Keychain app passwords; documents v1-vs-v2 command drift and oldest-mail recipes; triage.py/read-clean.py helpers.

skill-git-discipline.title: Git discipline for agent fleets
skill-git-discipline.summary_plain: Rules that stop many AI assistants working in the same code from trampling each other's changes.
skill-git-discipline.how_it_works: Worktree per session on agent/* branches, never-stage list, agent-ship for requested work straight to main, PR otherwise; pairs with commit_gate hook and agent-sweeper.

skill-handoff.title: Handoff skill
skill-handoff.summary_plain: When an AI session gets too long and forgetful, it writes a precise note so a fresh session can carry on.
skill-handoff.how_it_works: Fixed-section state file (goal, acceptance commands, verified done, ruled out, next action) written before context rot; overwritten not appended.

skill-pickup.title: Pickup skill
skill-pickup.summary_plain: The fresh AI session double-checks the previous one's notes before trusting them.
skill-pickup.how_it_works: Treats the handoff file as a claim: re-runs acceptance commands first, reconciles better/worse-than-claimed, honors 'ruled out'.

skill-homelab.title: Homelab operations skill
skill-homelab.summary_plain: The operating manual an AI uses to run and fix ~30 home-server services.
skill-homelab.how_it_works: Inventory + golden rules in SKILL.md, per-domain reference/*.md (networking, reverse proxy, LLM stack, backup, monitoring) read before acting.

skill-imagegen.title: imagegen skill (gateway + fallback + text overlay)
skill-imagegen.summary_plain: Generates cover art and illustrations, then adds clean title text on top.
skill-imagegen.how_it_works: gen.py tries the LiteLLM gateway then Together AI directly; overlay.sh adds text afterward because models garble text; model cost table and depiction rules.

skill-mealie.title: Mealie recipes skill
skill-mealie.summary_plain: Lets the AI plan meals, look up recipes and manage grocery lists.
skill-mealie.how_it_works: Mealie REST API with meal-plan.sh / shopping-list.sh helpers.

skill-mission-control.title: Mission Control participation skill
skill-mission-control.summary_plain: How each AI assistant claims work from the shared board and reports what it did so it shows up live.
skill-mission-control.how_it_works: Bearer-token agent API: claim with lease, renew, report, finish, log decisions with reason + alternatives not chosen.

skill-notify.title: notify: push alerts from any agent
skill-notify.summary_plain: Any AI session can buzz James's phone when a job finishes or breaks.
skill-notify.how_it_works: Home Assistant companion-app push; title/group default to the git repo name so alerts stack per project; tags replace earlier alerts; Uptime Kuma push monitors for dead-man heartbeats.

skill-open-relay.title: Open Relay / Open WebUI config pipe skill
skill-open-relay.summary_plain: Lets James change his self-hosted chat AI server's settings from his phone.
skill-open-relay.how_it_works: Round-trips Open WebUI's whole server config as one flat JSON via Open Relay's Admin export/import; owui-config.sh patches over HTTP; generated config-key reference.

skill-pim.title: PIM skill (calendula + cardamum)
skill-pim.summary_plain: Lets the AI check and edit calendars and contacts from the terminal.
skill-pim.how_it_works: Pimalaya calendula (CalDAV/Google) and cardamum (CardDAV/People) built from master, account names mirrored from himalaya; agenda.py/contact.py.

skill-reminders.title: reminders: Apple Reminders capture
skill-reminders.summary_plain: Say 'remind me' in any AI session and it lands on James's phone's to-do list.
skill-reminders.how_it_works: AppleScript against Reminders.app with a routing table (Reminders vs Mission Control vs GitHub issue); documents the TCC -1743 stale-denial gotcha in tmux.

skill-speko.title: Speko voice gateway skill
skill-speko.summary_plain: How the AI speaks, transcribes and makes voice calls through one voice-AI service.
skill-speko.how_it_works: Path table: LiteLLM models, HA announce script, a homelab Speko MCP bridge, Open WebUI tool server, or direct API.

skill-webcam.title: webcam: let the AI look at the desk
skill-webcam.summary_plain: The AI can take a photo with the desk webcam and actually look at it, to check a blinking light or a screen.
skill-webcam.how_it_works: go2rtc serves JPEG snapshots of a USB webcam; grab.sh with optional crop, then the agent Reads the image.

skill-applescript-automation.title: AppleScript automation skill
skill-applescript-automation.summary_plain: Lets the AI control Mac apps and the Ghostty terminal.
skill-applescript-automation.how_it_works: osascript recipes for Ghostty, window/UI scripting and multi-app workflows.

hook-continuity-autopilot.title: Continuity system: autopilot + context-budget relay
hook-continuity-autopilot.summary_plain: Keeps a long AI task moving without James typing 'yes go ahead' at every step, and passes the work to a fresh AI before the old one gets confused.
hook-continuity-autopilot.how_it_works: Stop hook tails the transcript: blocks the stop with 'next: X' while todos remain (capped hops, reset by continuity_reset.py when James types), triggers /handoff past a soft token budget at a green boundary or a hard budget regardless; relay_spawn.sh starts a new claude in tmux seeded with /pickup; /autopilot toggles via autopilot.sh. Fails open.

hook-commit-gate.title: commit_gate: no wandering off with a dirty tree
hook-commit-gate.summary_plain: Stops an AI from finishing a task while leaving its changes uncommitted.
hook-commit-gate.how_it_works: Stop hook that keys on files this session actually edited (parsed from transcript Edit/Write calls) rather than cwd git status, so it never fires on repos the agent only read; blocks and lets the model write the commit.

hook-mini-build-guard.title: Mini build guard
hook-mini-build-guard.summary_plain: Prevents AI assistants from running heavy builds on the home server and points them at the laptop instead.
hook-mini-build-guard.how_it_works: PreToolUse(Bash) regex deny-list (gradle, xcodebuild, cargo, JS build/test runners) active only on the server host; allows anything via air-run or MINI_BUILD_OK=1. Born from a load-27 incident.

hook-air-tts-stop-speech.title: Read every reply aloud (Kokoro TTS on the laptop)
hook-air-tts-stop-speech.summary_plain: Reads the AI's whole final answer out loud using a free voice model running on the laptop.
hook-air-tts-stop-speech.how_it_works: Stop hook detaches air_tts.py: Kokoro-82M on MLX on the MacBook Air over the tailnet, played on the Mini, lock-queued across sessions, falls back to Piper then macOS say, never to paid TTS; mute file; caches wavs for /replay.

hook-tmux-flash-pane.title: tmux pane flash on attention
hook-tmux-flash-pane.summary_plain: When an AI in a background terminal pane needs you, its border flashes pink then stays orange.
hook-tmux-flash-pane.how_it_works: Notification hook toggles tmux pane-border-style in a background subshell; skips the focused pane.

hook-tmux-rename.title: tmux window auto-titling
hook-tmux-rename.summary_plain: Names each terminal tab after what the AI is working on.
hook-tmux-rename.how_it_works: UserPromptSubmit hook slugifies Claude Code's ai-title from the transcript; an on-device apfel keyword covers the first turns before a title exists.

hook-mission-control-telemetry.title: Mission Control presence/telemetry hooks
hook-mission-control-telemetry.summary_plain: Every AI session automatically shows up live on the operations dashboard: when it starts, works, edits files and stops.
hook-mission-control-telemetry.how_it_works: Global SessionStart/PostToolUse/Stop/SessionEnd hooks post heartbeats and file-edit events to the Convex agent API; fail-open.

hook-afk-beacon.title: AFK beacon
hook-afk-beacon.summary_plain: Walk away from an AI task; when it's done your phone buzzes and opens a summary page you can have read aloud.
hook-afk-beacon.how_it_works: /afk writes a marker; the global Stop hook gate runs afk_beacon.py: transcript -> summary -> HTML page served over the tailnet -> Telegram push with the full closing message (HA push fallback).

statusline-telemetry.title: Status line: cost, rate limits, prompt-cache TTL
statusline-telemetry.summary_plain: A dashboard strip under the AI chat showing spend, usage limits and how long until its memory cache expires.
statusline-telemetry.how_it_works: uv script status line with cached Anthropic status/online probes, per-window rate-limit bars that dim when stale, prompt-cache hit rate + TTL countdown (shared with fleet-band), and per-session billing snapshots that feed claude-usage.

mod-auto-handoff.title: auto-handoff mod
mod-auto-handoff.summary_plain: If an AI task is still unfinished just before its cheap memory cache expires, it writes the hand-over note automatically.
mod-auto-handoff.how_it_works: Claude Code function-hook mod (TypeScript) times the prompt-cache TTL (60 or 5 min) minus lead time, forks a cache-served request to write handoff.md, optional phone push.

mod-fleet-band.title: fleet-band mod
mod-fleet-band.summary_plain: A band above the chat box showing which board task this AI owns, how many tasks are waiting, and how full its memory is.
mod-fleet-band.how_it_works: TSX mod reads Mission Control claim/lease, claimable queue and the prompt-cache/context cache written by the status line.

mod-phone-ping.title: phone-ping mod
mod-phone-ping.summary_plain: Buzzes the phone when a long AI turn finishes.
mod-phone-ping.how_it_works: Mod with a minMinutes threshold and /ping override; skips when the AFK beacon will already push.

mod-tts-replay.title: tts-replay mod
mod-tts-replay.summary_plain: /replay reads the last answer aloud again; /replay stop shuts it up.
mod-tts-replay.how_it_works: Replays cached wavs from speak_stop/air_tts per session; detaches playback and kills queued TTS on stop.

output-style-action-items.title: Action Items output style
output-style-action-items.summary_plain: Makes the AI keep prose short and put everything you need to do in a checklist.
output-style-action-items.how_it_works: Output style that extracts user actions, blockers and suggestions into a scannable block.

output-style-tts.title: TTS summary/completion output styles
output-style-tts.summary_plain: Makes the AI announce finished work out loud.
output-style-tts.how_it_works: Output styles that call the homelab LiteLLM TTS route.

cmd-artifact.title: /artifact: create a living HTML artifact
cmd-artifact.how_it_works: Front-end to the artifact skill with saving under personal/work trees.

cmd-artifact-publish.title: /artifact-publish
cmd-artifact-publish.summary_plain: Publishes a personal artifact to the public website.
cmd-artifact-publish.how_it_works: Copies into the GitHub Pages artifacts repo, regenerates index, commits, pushes, polls the URL; hard rule that work artifacts never publish.

cmd-artifact-expire.title: /artifact-expire
cmd-artifact-expire.summary_plain: Sets a date when a published page automatically disappears.
cmd-artifact-expire.how_it_works: Writes data-artifact-expires on <html>; a daily 03:00 launchd job git-rms expired files.

cmd-asciinema.title: /asciinema: terminal session to blog post
cmd-asciinema.summary_plain: Records a terminal session and publishes it as a blog post with a playable recording.
cmd-asciinema.how_it_works: asciinema record or tmux scrollback via tmux-to-cast.py, embedded player in a Jekyll post.

cmd-autopilot.title: /autopilot: auto-continue toggle
cmd-autopilot.summary_plain: Turns off the 'should I continue?' interruptions for one session.
cmd-autopilot.how_it_works: Calls autopilot.sh on|off|status against the continuity gate's per-session state.

cmd-claude-replay.title: /claude-replay: session to interactive replay post
cmd-claude-replay.summary_plain: Turns an AI coding session into an interactive replay published on the blog.
cmd-claude-replay.how_it_works: claude-replay export + Jekyll post; memory notes the redactor misses some cookies, so manual scan required.

cmd-mailgun.title: /mailgun admin
cmd-mailgun.summary_plain: Helps troubleshoot email sending across projects.
cmd-mailgun.how_it_works: Mailgun Admin API via curl/jq with key from env.

cmd-relay.title: /relay: Obsidian iPhone reply note
cmd-relay.summary_plain: Drops a note on James's phone where he can write back to the AI.
cmd-relay.how_it_works: Writes a session note into the iCloud Obsidian vault with an artifact link and a reply placeholder; agent reads it back after sync.

cmd-session-summary.title: /session-summary
cmd-session-summary.summary_plain: Makes a nice one-page summary of what was learned in the session and sends it to the phone.
cmd-session-summary.how_it_works: html skill output, Taildropped to the iPhone.

cmd-sessions.title: /sessions: search past sessions inline
cmd-sessions.summary_plain: Search and reopen any past AI conversation from inside the chat.
cmd-sessions.how_it_works: sqlite3 queries over the FTS5 session-index.db built by ~/.claude/bin/indexer.py.

cmd-todo.title: /todo
cmd-todo.summary_plain: Captures a stray to-do into Apple Reminders without derailing the task.

git-fleet-agent-merge.title: agent-merge: Jev-gated self-merge for agent branches
git-fleet-agent-merge.summary_plain: The one sanctioned way an AI may merge its own work: a script that reviews it first and refuses if it didn't show its work.
git-fleet-agent-merge.how_it_works: Two layers, fail-closed: mechanical checks (agent/* only, clean tree, merges cleanly, CI green, never-stage paths, size cap, opt-out file, due-diligence note with Verification) then seven yes/no TypeSafe Jev classifier questions with thresholds; Claude Code autoMode allow-rule carves out only this exact invocation.

git-fleet-worktree-sweeper-ship.title: Agent git fleet: worktrees, sweeper, ship
git-fleet-worktree-sweeper-ship.summary_plain: Gives every AI session its own copy of the code, then automatically opens reviews for finished work and cleans up.
git-fleet-worktree-sweeper-ship.how_it_works: agent-worktree makes ~/.claude/worktrees/<repo>/<slug> on agent/<slug>; launchd agent-sweeper publishes quiet clean branches as PRs and reaps merged worktrees across all repos; agent-ship rebases and fast-forward pushes requested work to main, never --force.

claude-config-versioning.title: ~/.claude config repo: deny-by-default .gitignore + secret pre-commit
claude-config-versioning.summary_plain: Keeps James's AI configuration under version control without ever committing transcripts or passwords.
claude-config-versioning.how_it_works: Allowlist .gitignore ('*' then re-include skills/agents/hooks...) so new runtime dirs are excluded by default; versioned pre-commit hook blocks forbidden paths and scans the staged diff for secret patterns (core.hooksPath).

fleet-evals-grader.title: Fleet run grader + Langfuse calibration
fleet-evals-grader.summary_plain: Every night, grades the unattended AI workers' runs against a rubric, and asks James to spot-check a sample so the grader stays honest.
fleet-evals-grader.how_it_works: grade_runs.py: deterministic safety checks over transcripts (forbidden commands, call caps, path scope) then a tool-less claude -p majority-of-3 judge with the policy as of run time (git); pushes traces/scores to Langfuse over OTLP; calibrate.py samples into a Langfuse annotation queue and pulls verdicts into labels.jsonl.

jobhunt-jobmail-feed.title: Job-mail feed agent
jobhunt-jobmail-feed.summary_plain: Every 5 minutes, sorts recruiter emails, pings the phone about the real ones, and files them on the board.
jobhunt-jobmail-feed.how_it_works: Gmail poll -> Jev classifier questions/thresholds (job_jev.py, ported byte-identical from the business drain) -> push + Mission Control role:jobhunt tasks; fail-closed retry.

jobhunt-interview-guard.title: Interview guard agent
jobhunt-interview-guard.summary_plain: Makes sure no interview is ever missed: invites go on the family calendar and the phone reminds you 30 and 10 minutes before.
jobhunt-interview-guard.how_it_works: launchd every 5 min: finds .ics invites in Gmail, adds job VEVENTs to the shared calendar with timezone conversion and conflict callouts, T-30/T-10 pushes, post-interview debrief cards; never deletes events.

jobhunt-linkedin-sweep.title: LinkedIn read-only sweep agent
jobhunt-linkedin-sweep.summary_plain: Checks LinkedIn messages and connection requests every 30 minutes so nothing sits unseen.
jobhunt-linkedin-sweep.how_it_works: Claude in Chrome with a tool allowlist that can only navigate/read (no click/type/script), reading the inbox via the compose page to avoid auto-opening threads.

jobhunt-sourcer-and-hygiene.title: Job-hunt sourcer + hygiene agents
jobhunt-sourcer-and-hygiene.summary_plain: Small robots that file new recruiter leads, flag duplicate submissions, nudge stale threads and merge duplicate cards.
jobhunt-sourcer-and-hygiene.how_it_works: sourcer.py (new recruiter -> task + CRM contact), dedup_checker.py (same end client via two vendors), nudge.py, task_dedup.py, waiting_on_you.py (they asked, you haven't answered in 24h); read/flag only, never reply.

jobhunt-vendor-clock.title: Vendor 48h artifact clock
jobhunt-vendor-clock.summary_plain: Grades staffing vendors on whether they produce something concrete within 48 hours, proposing grades for a human to confirm.
jobhunt-vendor-clock.how_it_works: Gmail thread forensics against a vendor ledger; proposes, never rewrites, because off-channel events (phone calls) are invisible to it.

jobhunt-jev-shadow-scorer.title: Jev shadow scorer for recruiter mail
jobhunt-jev-shadow-scorer.summary_plain: Tests an AI scoring of recruiter emails quietly, logging results without letting it decide anything yet.
jobhunt-jev-shadow-scorer.how_it_works: Shadow mode: scores and logs only; backtest showed the hand rubric at AUC 0.514 and a refit at 0.87 on 5 positives, so no thresholds until labels justify them.

jobhunt-scan-and-reply.title: Recruiter scan-and-reply (template-only)
jobhunt-scan-and-reply.summary_plain: Replies to new recruiter emails with a resume using fixed templates.
jobhunt-scan-and-reply.how_it_works: Fixed template replies only; no AI reads email bodies, as a prompt-injection defense; token read from a 0600 file.

jobhunt-profile-revamp-sweep.title: Profile A/B weekly inbound sweep
jobhunt-profile-revamp-sweep.summary_plain: Measures weekly whether a profile rewrite changed the kind of recruiter mail coming in.
jobhunt-profile-revamp-sweep.how_it_works: Keyword categorization of 7 days of inbound appended to an Obsidian experiment note; read-only.

call4me-followup-oneshot.title: One-shot scheduled agent follow-up
call4me-followup-oneshot.summary_plain: A one-time scheduled AI run that checked on phone calls it had placed and reported the outcome, then deleted itself.
call4me-followup-oneshot.how_it_works: launchd one-shot runs claude -p with an MCP config built at runtime from ~/.claude.json via jq so the key is never copied; date-guarded; self-removing.

chrome-debug-relaunch.title: Chrome remote-debug relaunch at login
chrome-debug-relaunch.summary_plain: Makes sure Chrome always starts in a mode the AI can connect to.
chrome-debug-relaunch.how_it_works: Login launchd job restarts Chrome if DevToolsActivePort is missing (Chrome 145+ toggle behavior).

cli-sessions-explorer.title: Claude Code session explorer (FTS5)
cli-sessions-explorer.summary_plain: Search every past AI conversation across all projects and jump back into one.
cli-sessions-explorer.how_it_works: indexer.py loads all transcripts into SQLite FTS5 (session-index.db); sessions/tui.py/sessions-tui.py TUI and the /sessions command query it.

cli-claude-usage.title: claude-usage: spend rolled up by project and org
cli-claude-usage.summary_plain: Shows how much AI usage each project and company cost.
cli-claude-usage.how_it_works: billing/rollup.py joins per-render status-line billing snapshots (the only durable cost record) with transcripts' per-message token usage on session_id, attributing by cwd to orgs.

cli-cc-session.title: cc-session: resolve session handles
cli-cc-session.summary_plain: Turns a short session nickname into the full path and resume command so one AI can read what another did.
cli-cc-session.how_it_works: Matches 8-hex id prefixes or /rename titles across ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl via jq on customTitle/aiTitle.

cli-rea-sync.title: rea-sync
cli-rea-sync.summary_plain: Moves files to the laptop for heavy reverse-engineering and brings results back.
cli-rea-sync.how_it_works: rsync to ~/rea-work on the Air; identical absolute home path on both machines lets paths be passed verbatim to the remote MCP.

cli-devenv-helpers.title: devenv-* Keychain secret helpers
cli-devenv-helpers.summary_plain: One locked vault for all ~41 API keys, with commands to add or read a secret without it appearing on screen.
cli-devenv-helpers.how_it_works: zsh functions over one Keychain item holding base64 NAME=VALUE lines; devenv-set prompts hidden and confirms with a fingerprint; devenv-get -c copies to clipboard.

cli-gog-reauth.title: gog-reauth: phone-friendly OAuth
cli-gog-reauth.summary_plain: Re-logs in a Google CLI tool from the phone with one tap instead of copying a giant link.
cli-gog-reauth.how_it_works: tailscale serve fronts the CLI's localhost OAuth callback with a real cert; serves a tiny one-tap page because pasting the 2.3 KB auth URL on a phone corrupts it.

cli-seed-headless-tokens.title: seed-headless-tokens
cli-seed-headless-tokens.summary_plain: Sets up the login tokens that remote terminal sessions need, entered hidden at the console.
cli-seed-headless-tokens.how_it_works: Writes 0600 token files under ~/.config because ssh sessions cannot read the login Keychain; hidden prompt, never touches history.

cli-claude-prune-stale-projects.title: claude-prune-stale-projects
cli-claude-prune-stale-projects.summary_plain: Cleans out dead folders from Claude Code's settings file.
cli-claude-prune-stale-projects.how_it_works: Dry-run-by-default pruner of ~/.claude.json projects whose dirs no longer exist; refuses while any session is live because Claude rewrites the file on exit.

cli-air-run.title: air-run
cli-air-run.summary_plain: Runs test suites on the laptop instead of the cramped home server.
cli-air-run.how_it_works: ssh wrapper that syncs and executes on the MacBook Air; the build-guard hook points agents here.

cli-hc-run.title: hc-run / hc-sync / hc-wrap (Healthchecks wrappers)
cli-hc-run.summary_plain: Every scheduled job reports to a monitor when it starts, finishes or fails.
cli-hc-run.how_it_works: Pings /start, passes stdout through untouched, then pings /<exit-code> with last 100 KB of output; auto-creates checks, hc-sync sets schedules.

cli-splogs.title: splogs (screenpipe logs across machines)
cli-splogs.summary_plain: One view of a screen-recording tool's logs from two computers.
cli-splogs.how_it_works: Aggregates six log locations across Mini and Air; written after a crash loop went unnoticed.

cli-dev-tunnel.title: dev-tunnel
cli-dev-tunnel.summary_plain: Opens the home server's dev websites on the laptop.
cli-dev-tunnel.how_it_works: Builds an ssh -L command for a list of ports.

cli-tmux-to-cast.title: tmux-to-cast
cli-tmux-to-cast.summary_plain: Turns a terminal's scrollback into a replayable recording.
cli-tmux-to-cast.how_it_works: Converts tmux pane scrollback into asciicast v2 with synthetic timing.

mcp-screenpipe.title: screenpipe / screenpipe-air MCP launcher (James wrapper)
mcp-screenpipe.summary_plain: Lets the AI search what was on screen or said, on either computer.
mcp-screenpipe.how_it_works: One launcher script per backend (live Mini, Air replica); screenpipe itself is third-party. Local-scope only in a few projects. Registration: stdio: homelab screenpipe-mcp-launcher <api-url>.

mcp-rea-air.title: rea / rea-air (remote REA over ssh stdio)
mcp-rea-air.summary_plain: Runs the reverse-engineering toolkit on the laptop so risky binaries never run on the server.
mcp-rea-air.how_it_works: REA is third-party; James's part is the ssh-stdio remote registration, local scope, and rea-sync staging. Registration: stdio: npx rea-agents@6.3.0 mcp locally; ssh -T BatchMode to the laptop for rea-air.

mcp-speko-bridge.title: Speko MCP bridge (James-built)
mcp-speko-bridge.summary_plain: Voice-AI tools (agents, numbers, transcripts, credits) for the AI.
mcp-speko-bridge.how_it_works: Python MCP wrapping the Speko API in the homelab speko-bridge container. Registration: homelab speko-bridge speko_mcp.py (used by Open WebUI/skills).

tech-keychain-base64-env.title: One Keychain item for all shell secrets (base64 or bust)
tech-keychain-base64-env.summary_plain: Keep every API key in one locked vault instead of in shell config files, without slowing down new terminals.
tech-keychain-base64-env.how_it_works: Store base64 of NAME=VALUE lines in a single Keychain item (one ~32ms read vs ~1.3s for 41 items); base64 is load-bearing because `security -w` silently switches to hex when data has newlines, which also fools naive round-trip checks.

tech-omni-token-pinned-account.title: Omni-token + pinned account_id
tech-omni-token-pinned-account.summary_plain: Give AI agents one all-powerful cloud key, but make every project refuse to deploy anywhere except its own account.
tech-omni-token-pinned-account.how_it_works: Broad Cloudflare user token = capability; explicit account_id in each wrangler config = safety, since wrangler refuses other accounts. Verify /accounts before first deploy.

tech-obsidian-message-bus.title: Obsidian vault as an iPhone<->agent message bus
tech-obsidian-message-bus.summary_plain: When typing long messages into the AI from a phone breaks, write them in a notes app that syncs instead.
tech-obsidian-message-bus.how_it_works: SSH TUI paste strips newlines, so the agent writes a session note with a paste placeholder into the iCloud-synced vault; the user fills it on the phone and says 'check it'. Caveat learned: a file landing in iCloud can never notify the phone.

tech-min-release-age.title: 48-hour minimum release age across npm, pnpm and bun
tech-min-release-age.summary_plain: Refuse to install any software package published less than two days ago, to dodge poisoned releases.
tech-min-release-age.how_it_works: npm min-release-age=2 (days, ~/.npmrc), pnpm minimum-release-age=2880 (minutes, separate rc to avoid npm warnings), bun minimumReleaseAge=172800 (seconds, bunfig) — three keys, three units, three files.

tech-rea-offload-to-laptop.title: Offload heavy/risky reverse engineering to a second machine
tech-rea-offload-to-laptop.summary_plain: Run untrusted programs and heavy analysis on the laptop, never on the server holding the passwords.
tech-rea-offload-to-laptop.how_it_works: Same MCP registered twice: local for metadata reads and runtime attach, ssh-stdio remote for decompile/observe; identical home paths make file paths portable; single-arch lipo before Ghidra.

tech-mcp-local-scope-diet.title: Scope heavy MCP servers to projects, not the user
tech-mcp-local-scope-diet.summary_plain: Only load big AI plug-ins in the projects that use them, saving memory in every other session.
tech-mcp-local-scope-diet.how_it_works: Moved REA and screenpipe MCPs from user to local scope (~250 MB per session for a tool used once); re-register via `claude mcp add-json -s local` with jq from ~/.claude.json.

tech-ios-html-serve-over-tailnet.title: View local HTML on iPhone by serving it
tech-ios-html-serve-over-tailnet.summary_plain: iPhone's Files app won't run interactive web pages, so serve them from the computer instead.
tech-ios-html-serve-over-tailnet.how_it_works: iOS Files preview runs no JavaScript and Safari isn't an .html handler; `python3 -m http.server --bind 0.0.0.0` and open the tailnet hostname.

tech-tailnet-hostname-not-localhost.title: Give phone-reachable URLs, never localhost
tech-tailnet-hostname-not-localhost.summary_plain: When the AI shares a link, it should be one that works from your phone.
tech-tailnet-hostname-not-localhost.how_it_works: Default to the MagicDNS hostname; TLS certs from Tailscale only match that name, so localhost or raw IPs break strict TLS.

tech-remote-friendly-auth.title: Prefer device/remote auth flows over localhost OAuth
tech-remote-friendly-auth.summary_plain: Logging in to tools should work when you're only holding your phone.
tech-remote-friendly-auth.how_it_works: Use device-code/non-interactive flows; where a localhost callback is unavoidable, front it with tailscale serve and a one-tap page (gog-reauth).

tech-tmux-aqua-keychain.title: Run the tmux server in the GUI session so ssh panes can read Keychain
tech-tmux-aqua-keychain.summary_plain: Lets remote terminal sessions use stored passwords and browser tools as if you were at the desk.
tech-tmux-aqua-keychain.how_it_works: ssh shells get 'User interaction is not allowed' from Keychain; start tmux via launchd in the Aqua session and always attach; grant FDA to tmux since TCC now attributes to it.

tech-launchd-tcc-responsible-process.title: launchd daemons need their own TCC grants
tech-launchd-tcc-responsible-process.summary_plain: Mac background services need their own privacy permissions; testing from a terminal lies.
tech-launchd-tcc-responsible-process.how_it_works: TCC grants are per binary path+cdhash; launchd makes the daemon its own responsible process; Mic/Camera rows only appear after requestAccess, so ship a tiny launcher that requests then spawns the real binary.

tech-verify-check-can-fail.title: Make a check fail on purpose before trusting it
tech-verify-check-can-fail.summary_plain: A test that says 'all clear' means nothing until you've seen it catch a planted problem.
tech-verify-check-can-fail.how_it_works: Plant a canary, watch it get caught, remove it, watch it go quiet; three same-shape false-clean checks in one day motivated it.

tech-taildrop-pitfalls.title: Taildrop pitfalls: false success and iOS jetsam
tech-taildrop-pitfalls.summary_plain: Sending files to your phone can say 'sent' when it wasn't, and big files can knock the phone off the network.
tech-taildrop-pitfalls.how_it_works: `tailscale file cp` exits 0 on failed delivery and offline phones look present; iOS network-extension memory floor grows with uptime, so toggle Tailscale before big transfers.

tech-flat-rate-vs-metered-claude-routes.title: Separate flat-rate and metered Claude routes in an LLM gateway
tech-flat-rate-vs-metered-claude-routes.summary_plain: Keep the subscription-covered AI and the pay-per-use AI clearly separate so you don't get surprise bills.
tech-flat-rate-vs-metered-claude-routes.how_it_works: Unsuffixed gateway models carry no api_key and only accept a client's own OAuth token (cost 0); '-api' models use a metered key; leaving ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set silently switches Claude Code to metered billing.

tech-orbstack-gotchas.title: OrbStack container gotchas on a Mac server
tech-orbstack-gotchas.summary_plain: Hard-won traps running ~30 containers on a Mac.
tech-orbstack-gotchas.how_it_works: host network mode proxies TCP only (UDP vanishes); host-side sqlite .backup of a bind-mounted DB wedges the container over virtiofs; SQLite on APFS bind mounts corrupts (use named volumes); VM memory ratchets to its cap; external /Volumes mounts go stale.

tech-kuma-timeout-overflow.title: Uptime Kuma long-interval timeout overflow
tech-kuma-timeout-overflow.summary_plain: A monitoring tool reports false outages for hourly checks unless you set a timeout.
tech-kuma-timeout-overflow.how_it_works: Interval >=3600s with default timeout overflows Node setTimeout and aborts instantly; always set an explicit timeout.

tech-dev-tools-before-browser-automation.title: Dev tools first, browser automation last
tech-dev-tools-before-browser-automation.summary_plain: Talk to a service's real API before making an AI click around a website.
tech-dev-tools-before-browser-automation.how_it_works: Lift bearer tokens/endpoints from devtools and call the API; browser automation was fragile and wasted hours.

tech-interactive-in-tmux-split.title: Interactive prompts go in a tmux split, not the chat
tech-interactive-in-tmux-split.summary_plain: When a command needs your password, the AI opens a side pane for you to type it.
tech-interactive-in-tmux-split.how_it_works: Agent opens a tmux split for sudo/login flows instead of asking the user to run commands inline.

tech-shared-checkout-verify-deploy.title: In shared checkouts, prove your deploy landed
tech-shared-checkout-verify-deploy.summary_plain: When several AIs share code, 'deploy succeeded' doesn't mean your change is the one live.
tech-shared-checkout-verify-deploy.how_it_works: Concurrent sessions deploy the same Worker; probe production after deploy; dirty files and git authorship can't identify an owner, which motivated worktree-per-session.

tech-no-destructive-api-probing.title: Never include delete endpoints when probing an API
tech-no-destructive-api-probing.summary_plain: When exploring an unknown API, the AI must never try delete or remove calls.
tech-no-destructive-api-probing.how_it_works: Learned after an exploratory probe deleted a production playlist; probes are read-only by rule.

tech-pixel-check-black-streams.title: HTTP 200 isn't 'working' for video streams
tech-pixel-check-black-streams.summary_plain: A video link can answer 'OK' and still show a black screen.
tech-pixel-check-black-streams.how_it_works: HEAD/status probes miss empty/black streams; sample frames and pixel-check before marking channels alive.

tech-workerd-vi-mock.title: vi.mock doesn't intercept ESM in Workers vitest pool
tech-workerd-vi-mock.summary_plain: A testing trick that silently doesn't work for Cloudflare Workers.
tech-workerd-vi-mock.how_it_works: With @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers, spy on class prototypes instead of vi.mock for ESM imports.

tech-rdap-not-availability.title: RDAP 404 means unregistered, not available
tech-rdap-not-availability.summary_plain: A domain lookup saying 'not found' doesn't mean you can buy it.
tech-rdap-not-availability.how_it_works: Registry premium/reserved status is invisible to RDAP; confirm with a registrar checker.

tech-reminders-automation-vs-data-tcc.title: Apple Reminders: Automation permission, not data permission
tech-reminders-automation-vs-data-tcc.summary_plain: Why an AI can't add reminders even when it seems allowed, and the workaround.
tech-reminders-automation-vs-data-tcc.how_it_works: kTCCServiceReminders data grant is necessary but not sufficient; AppleScript needs Automation (-1743); fallback is creating a VTODO over iCloud CalDAV.

tech-narrow-rails-autonomy.title: Autonomous agents get one narrow lane that ships
tech-narrow-rails-autonomy.summary_plain: Unattended AIs work best with one small job they can finish without asking, not broad advisory reports.
tech-narrow-rails-autonomy.how_it_works: Scope scheduled agents to a single lane with explicit ship authority; pairs with per-role eval rubrics.

tech-shadow-mode-before-gating.title: Run a classifier in shadow mode before it can gate
tech-shadow-mode-before-gating.summary_plain: Let a new AI judge watch silently until there's evidence it's right.
tech-shadow-mode-before-gating.how_it_works: Log scores only; a hand rubric backtested at chance (AUC 0.514) and a tiny-sample refit had a wide CI, so thresholds wait for labels; contrast with fail-closed gates like agent-merge.

tech-transcript-redaction-before-publish.title: Manually scan session replays before publishing
tech-transcript-redaction-before-publish.summary_plain: Auto-redaction of AI session recordings misses some login cookies, so check by hand.
tech-transcript-redaction-before-publish.how_it_works: claude-replay's redactor missed site session cookies; grep for cookie names/tokens before publishing scraper sessions (a leaked replay was later removed).

tech-headless-ssh-token-files.title: Headless shells need 0600 token files
tech-headless-ssh-token-files.summary_plain: Remote terminal sessions can't open the Mac's password vault, so they need separate locked-down token files.
tech-headless-ssh-token-files.how_it_works: Keychain is unreadable from ssh security sessions; seed 0600 files at the console with hidden prompts; Claude Code's OAuth token lives in its own Keychain item that /login doesn't update.

tech-air-local-inference.title: Put local inference on the idle laptop, not the server
tech-air-local-inference.summary_plain: Use the laptop's chip for free speech and small AI models so the home server stays responsive.
tech-air-local-inference.how_it_works: Kokoro TTS on MLX and a small Ollama model on the Air, reached over the tailnet with fallbacks when it sleeps; caffeinate LaunchAgent keeps it reachable on AC.

tech-template-only-replies-injection-def.title: Template-only auto-replies as a prompt-injection defense
tech-template-only-replies-injection-def.summary_plain: An auto-responder that never lets an AI read the incoming email can't be tricked by it.
tech-template-only-replies-injection-def.how_it_works: Fixed templates keyed on metadata; no model ingests bodies.

vault-llm-wiki.title: James personal wiki (Karpathy-style LLM wiki)
vault-llm-wiki.summary_plain: A personal knowledge base about James that AI assistants read to understand him and keep up to date on their own.
vault-llm-wiki.how_it_works: Plain markdown vault with a SCHEMA.md contract (frontmatter types, index.md registry, wiki-links) so any LLM (local Gemma "subconscious" daemon, Claude Code) can ingest and maintain pages; iCloud syncs to phone.

vault-schema-doc.how_it_works: Directory layout + YAML frontmatter types + maintenance rules (ingest-update not duplicate, freshness dates, pruning); names Gemma as primary maintainer.

obsidian-cli-workflow.title: Obsidian CLI workflow (two modes: URI vs direct file writes)
obsidian-cli-workflow.summary_plain: How to add notes to Obsidian from scripts and AI agents without opening the app.
obsidian-cli-workflow.how_it_works: Contrasts obsidian-cli (obsidian:// URI dispatch that silently no-ops if the app is closed) with direct file writes into the iCloud vault folder, which is the reliable agent path.

agent-scratchpad-idea.title: Agent Scratchpad: a moderated GET-addressable commons for sandboxed LLM agents
agent-scratchpad-idea.summary_plain: An idea for a public message board that locked-down AI agents could use to coordinate, built so the humans can always watch.

ideas-scratch-list.how_it_works: Unstructured bullet list; feeds ideas/ pages and the site _ideas parking lot.

loop-engineering-clipping.summary_plain: A saved article about making AI agents prompt themselves in loops instead of a human prompting them each turn.
loop-engineering-clipping.how_it_works: Clipped X/Twitter long-post: five building blocks (timers, sub-agents, self-feeding queues) above the agent harness. Informs James's Mission Control / director fleet design.

homelab-disaster-recovery-runbook.title: Homelab disaster-recovery runbook (encrypted R2 backups)
homelab-disaster-recovery-runbook.summary_plain: Step-by-step instructions, readable from a phone, for getting everything back if the home server dies or email is lost.
homelab-disaster-recovery-runbook.how_it_works: Nightly encrypted (age) off-site backups to Cloudflare R2 via rclone, restore-tested; scenario-based runbook (lost email / one corrupt service / full rebuild); keys deliberately kept out of the synced vault.

vault-project-openclaw.summary_plain: Notes on an AI gateway that routes requests across several AI providers with automatic fallbacks.
vault-project-openclaw.how_it_works: Primary Kimi K2.5 via NVIDIA, fallback Groq Kimi K2 -> Qwen3-32B -> local Ollama; skills for Mealie/Home Assistant/eBay MCP; self-heal hooks.

vault-project-llm-red-team.summary_plain: Notes on tests that measure how easily AI chat models leak secrets or break their safety rules.
vault-project-llm-red-team.how_it_works: arena/personas/refusals test suites against Gemma 4 censored vs abliterated, with defense-rate table; subconscious background daemon.

vault-skills-ai-ml.title: AI/ML and technical skills pages
vault-skills-ai-ml.summary_plain: A self-description of James's AI and engineering skills.
vault-skills-ai-ml.how_it_works: Lists local LLM deployment, abliteration, red-teaming, MoE, tool-calling proxy, model routing, MCP.

record-both-sides-interview-audio.title: Recording both sides of a remote call on macOS (AirPods)
record-both-sides-interview-audio.summary_plain: How to record both your voice and the other person's voice during a video call on a Mac.
record-both-sides-interview-audio.how_it_works: Explains why QuickTime only captures one input device (AirPods split into separate input/output devices) and how to build an aggregate/multi-output device so both sides land in one recording.

work-court-docket-watcher.title: Split court-docket watcher (homelab fetch + Worker parse/watermark)
work-court-docket-watcher.summary_plain: Checks a public court docket every few minutes and pings your phone when something new is filed.
work-court-docket-watcher.how_it_works: Two halves on purpose: a launchd job fetches the court API and pushes via a tailnet-only notifier; a Worker parses/classifies and keeps snapshot+watermark in KV, polling itself only as a fallback; ingest/pending/ack protocol prevents duplicate pushes.

work-tv-bug-report-relay.title: APK-safe bug-report relay Worker
work-tv-bug-report-relay.summary_plain: Lets a TV app send bug reports to the support desk without hiding any passwords inside the app.
work-tv-bug-report-relay.how_it_works: Worker accepts anonymous POSTs from the app and forwards as email into the helpdesk's email-to-ticket path, because shipping helpdesk credentials in an APK publishes them to anyone with apktool.

work-gam-runbook.title: Multi-domain Google Workspace administration runbook
work-gam-runbook.summary_plain: A how-to for managing a company's whole Google email/accounts setup from the command line.
work-gam-runbook.how_it_works: GAM7 runbook with the multi-domain gotcha (primary domain differs from the brand you think) and domain-scoped queries, recovery and security notes.

work-school-rag-labs.title: Magic-link-gated RAG 'ask the organization' tool
work-school-rag-labs.summary_plain: An internal website where volunteers can ask questions and get answers drawn from years of meeting notes and bylaws.
work-school-rag-labs.how_it_works: Astro on Workers with allowlisted magic-link auth, Vectorize + Workers AI embeddings, custom chunker, entity extraction, a wiki editor and a competency-graph view; same index reused with different prompts for onboarding bots.

work-mention-monitor-reconstructed.title: Social mention monitor reconstructed from its deployed bundle
work-mention-monitor-reconstructed.summary_plain: Each day it checks Reddit, Bluesky and news feeds for mentions of an organization and saves the new ones.
work-mention-monitor-reconstructed.how_it_works: Cron Worker storing mentions in D1; the source was never committed, so the repo was rebuilt from the deployed bundle kept verbatim for diffing (Reddit app-only OAuth since unauthenticated JSON is 403).

work-school-effect-analysis.title: School effectiveness causal analysis (value-added, diff-in-diff, synthetic control)
work-school-effect-analysis.summary_plain: A statistics study of whether a school and a new reading curriculum are helping students, using only public data.
work-school-effect-analysis.how_it_works: Citywide panel from public suppressed aggregates; value-added residuals, staggered-rollout difference-in-differences for curriculum, synthetic control for a leadership transition; documented null hypotheses and ethics framing.

client-gov-contract-radar.title: Government contract opportunity radar with 3D embedding map
client-gov-contract-radar.summary_plain: Finds government contracting opportunities that match a business and shows them on an interactive 3D map of similar opportunities.
client-gov-contract-radar.how_it_works: SAM.gov ingest, Voyage embeddings in pgvector for semantic search and recommendations, UMAP projection rendered with React Three Fiber, Stripe subscriptions.

mc-file-claim-hook.title: PostToolUse file soft-claim hook for agent collision detection
mc-file-claim-hook.summary_plain: Every time an AI session edits a file, it quietly tells the dashboard, so two sessions editing the same file get flagged.
mc-file-claim-hook.how_it_works: Claude Code PostToolUse(Edit|Write|...) hook reads the tool payload from stdin, posts a short-lived soft claim; fail-open with a short timeout so the hub being down never blocks work.

mc-fleet-runner.title: Schedules-produce, runners-pull fleet execution
mc-fleet-runner.summary_plain: Scheduled chores become tasks on a board and a background runner picks them up and hands them to an AI agent with a time limit.
mc-fleet-runner.how_it_works: Cron only writes task rows; a launchd runner claims over REST, invokes headless claude -p with a wall-clock ceiling, then finishes or releases-as-blocked with a push.

mc-omnifeed.title: Omnifeed: one inbound log across channels with recipient-domain gate
mc-omnifeed.summary_plain: Collects every customer/vendor message from all channels into one feed an agent can triage.
mc-omnifeed.how_it_works: Polls a shared forwarding inbox and keeps a message only if the original To/Delivered-To matches an allowlisted org domain, dropping everything else before storage; org is a required field so adding orgs is config, not migration.

mc-harness-absorption.title: Mission Control to agent-harness plugin migration
mc-harness-absorption.summary_plain: A plan and in-progress code to fold the dashboard into an AI agent runtime as a plugin.
mc-harness-absorption.how_it_works: Out-of-tree plugin bundle with a typed contract and store package replacing Convex; locked-decisions handoff doc.

family-desk-dial.title: Round desk display: 'leave now' school-run instrument
family-desk-dial.summary_plain: A small round counter display, given as a birthday gift, that tells you when to walk out the door for school drop-off.
family-desk-dial.how_it_works: ESPHome firmware on an M5Stack Dial showing six live readings on a 240px circle with one rotary control, plus a simulator config.

family-podcast-publisher.title: Hand-written script to TTS podcast episode injector
family-podcast-publisher.summary_plain: Turns a written script into a spoken podcast episode on a private feed.
family-podcast-publisher.how_it_works: Splits text on paragraph boundaries under the 4096-char speech cap, synthesizes via an OpenAI-compatible gateway, writes audio plus an atomic newest-first metadata row matching the feed's own store.
